LATEST OPERATIONAL BUILD

One site. Every lane. No dead pages.

Carnival Careers connects the home-page video, categorized navigation, work and culture pages, playable music, purchasable beat licenses, Shopify commerce, plane/car/boat travel, affiliate links, auto-money funnels, child-care coverage, business acquisition and land prospecting.

ONE WOMAN • ONE FAMILY • ONE CITY • ONE ECONOMIC ENGINE

One woman opens the story. One family makes it matter. One city turns it into an economy.

Every city begins with a living woman whose contribution deserves more light. She chooses a Carnival-culture family, and they meet at dinner. From that table, her history and the family's real life lead naturally into work, housing, food, mobility, business, ownership and the city around them. Those needs activate the Carnival Careers engine in real time. The arena concert is not the beginning of the story — it is the victory lap, and it always comes last.

65-city modelOne woman + one familyHousing + workBusiness enginesTelevision + live culture
01 Story + engine +
The human story and the business model are the same moving story.

Carnival Careers does not invent a television story and then hunt for a business underneath it. The woman introduces us to a family. Dinner reveals what matters. The family's needs make the economic engine visible: a home has to be secured, work has to be real, mobility and child care have to function, food and commerce have to move, local partners have to show up, and the city has to see the change. Television follows that movement. The arena gathers everybody around what has already happened.

01

Woman of the city

A living woman whose contribution deserves fuller recognition becomes the doorway into the city.

02

She chooses a family

A Carnival-culture family gives the episode real stakes, real relationships and a real next move.

03

Dinner opens everything

Food and conversation reveal her history, the family's pressure points, the city and what progress would actually mean.

04

Home + work become tangible

Housing, paid work, training, child care and ownership pathways turn the story into something measurable.

05

The businesses start moving

Food, sponsors, vendors, mobility, travel, music, commerce and capital solve real needs while creating revenue and assets.

06

The city becomes the episode

Transit, civic activation, Carnival culture and filmed media take the family's progress into public view.

07

Arena last. Then next city.

The concert is the public celebration. The assets, relationships, jobs and media remain, and the engine moves to the next city.

Planning-stage platform. Employment, financing, housing, sponsorship, travel, artist and venue outcomes require their own executed documents. The point of the Project page is to show how the pieces connect without pretending that one agreement automatically creates another.

02 Industry engines +
One family story activates multiple industries.

Each engine has its own economics and its own job, but they share the same audience, city, family story and operating infrastructure. That is what turns Carnival Careers from a single event into a repeatable platform.

Live entertainment

The audience engine. Arena-scale culture creates attention, ticket inventory, sponsor inventory and the public finale.

Sponsorship

The commercial-margin engine. Brands fund useful, visible roles tied to audience experience, family value and media.

Real estate

The asset engine. Property turns cultural attention into a durable housing, collateral and ownership story.

Workforce

The human infrastructure. Paid roles, training, scheduling and documented income help the household move forward.

Finance + performing notes

The finance engine. Asset finance, structured capital and note income are separate from event revenue and need their own controls.

Television + media

The IP engine. The operating work becomes repeatable filmed intellectual property, sponsor inventory and distribution value.

Food + restaurants

The table-to-commerce engine. Dinner opens the story while restaurants, groceries and food partners create useful commercial participation.

SweetEV + mobility

The movement engine. Vehicle access, rideshare and household mobility connect work, filming and city movement.

Cruise + travel

The destination engine. Group movement carries audience, culture, sponsors and future episodes from city to city.

Music

The soundtrack engine. Original recordings, artists and licensing extend the culture beyond the live event.

Commerce

The transaction engine. Shopify, licensing, products, referrals and other tracked offers convert attention into purchases.

Vendors + marketplace

The local-business engine. Merchants and service partners plug local commerce into the same audience and city activation.

The engines are connected operationally, not automatically commingled financially. Capital, debt, sponsor receipts, restricted grants, commercial sales and asset proceeds keep the controls required by their own agreements.

03 Professional forms +
Firm up the people who make each city executable.

The goal is not a directory of names. It is a delivery bench: who owns the deliverable, what it costs, how fast it can close, and what dependency it clears.

INVESTORS

Back the company that takes the Carnival Careers model city to city.

We combine housing, work, operating businesses, Caribbean culture, live events, travel, commerce and filmed media. Investors can back the operating company or a specific asset deal — without pretending those are the same investment.

Start a private conversationRequest diligence
What you are buying into

One repeatable city engine.

A family story becomes housing and work. The city becomes the stage. The event creates attention. Media extends it. Commerce, sponsorship, travel and business activity turn that attention into revenue. Then the model moves to the next city.

Your lane

Choose the part you actually want to invest in.

01

Operating-company equity

The current company-level conversation is a C$3M seed round for the repeatable media, live-experience, commerce, distribution and operating system. Counsel has discussed a parent company with operating subsidiaries as one possible structure; final securities terms are not yet set.

For seed, media, culture, commerce and platform investors
02

Property and acquisition capital

Real estate is financed separately. Each property or portfolio is meant to stand on its own purchase price, appraisal, lender terms, equity requirement, release schedule and exit. The current Vic Towns conversation is active but still financing- and documentation-gated.

For real-estate equity, bridge and JV capital
03

Operating-business acquisitions

Grocery and other cash-flow businesses can sit beside the city platform as operating assets. Seller financing, institutional debt and purchaser capital are negotiated at the business level rather than hidden inside the entertainment budget.

For acquisition and cash-flow investors
04

City-by-city strategic capital

As the rollout travels, local capital can participate in a specific city, asset, operating business or launch rather than funding the entire 65-city vision at once.

For family offices, local partners and strategic co-investors

LENDERS

Finance the asset. See the repayment path. Keep the story separate.

Carnival Careers needs lenders who can underwrite real estate, business acquisitions and other defined facilities on normal credit logic. We bring the wider platform; the loan still has to make sense on collateral, cash flow, equity, controls and exit.

Send your credit boxSee diligence path
What you are lending into

Defined facilities, not one giant mixed ask.

Property debt should be paid by property economics. Business-acquisition debt should be paid by the business. Event and media revenue can strengthen the broader company, but it is not used as a substitute for sound underwriting.

Lending lanes

Where a lender can fit.

01

Senior real-estate financing

Acquisition or refinance facilities sized against the lower of acceptable LTV, LTC, DSCR/debt-yield and sale-release constraints. The current Toronto lender conversation is centered on a Vic Towns unit-block acquisition with the final property schedule and closing economics still being confirmed.

Banks, credit unions, mortgage funds and institutional lenders
02

Bridge and private mortgage capital

For deposits, timing gaps, renovations or acquisition closings where a short-duration facility can be secured, documented and taken out by sale, refinance or permanent debt.

Private lenders, MICs and bridge funds
03

CMHC / insured multifamily financing

Where a property qualifies, affordability, accessibility, energy performance, rent roll, building condition, borrower strength and reserves can be packaged for lender and CMHC review. No insured financing is called approved before it is approved.

CMHC-capable lenders and multifamily specialists
04

Business-acquisition debt

Operating businesses can use a mix of purchaser equity, institutional debt and seller VTB. Current acquisition work has included seller-financing structures where the seller carries a large portion of the price.

Commercial lenders and acquisition-finance specialists
Current file

What the lender needs to get to a real yes.

The current Vic Towns dialogue remains active. The broker side has asked for a stronger deposit and has encouraged a same-day closing of the unit block. We are not representing those requests as funded until the capital and credit package actually supports them.

Collateral and valuation

Final unit schedule, purchase contracts, appraisal instructions, title/status, legal review and asset-specific due diligence.

Credit structure

Maximum leverage, equity requirement, rate, fees, term, amortization, recourse, reserves, covenants and closing timeline.

Release and repayment

Unit-by-unit release prices where applicable, controlled funds flow and senior lender repayment before investor profit distributions.

Current lender relationships

We are already in the market.

CIBCA financing-screening conversation is scheduled for September 11. It is a screening discussion, not an approval.
Prime FinanceMalcolm Ramsay confirmed that his firm underwrites, structures and funds residential and commercial mortgages; the immediate request has been narrowed to property financing.
Seller-financed acquisitionsCurrent business-acquisition work includes vendors willing to discuss meaningful VTB structures, reducing the amount that must come from an institutional lender at closing.
TRC SolarTRC Solar has opened a property-energy discussion around solar/EV infrastructure without upfront capital or added debt, subject to site-specific review. That can reduce capex pressure; it is not presented as mortgage proceeds.

Lend with us city by city.

As Carnival Careers travels, we want a lender network that can handle local real estate, operating businesses, multifamily, bridge needs, fleet/equipment and other financeable assets without forcing every city into the same credit product.

Work with us

Give us the credit box first.

Tell us what you finance, where you lend, your typical facility size, leverage, pricing, recourse and what you need to issue a term sheet. That is more useful than asking for a generic deck.

Do not send personal KYC, banking credentials or sensitive borrower information through this public form. Those belong in the lender's secure process.

PROFESSIONAL SERVICES

Help us close the work in Toronto — then come with us around the world.

How we work

Own an outcome.

We want scope, fee, timing, dependencies and a named person responsible. The best service partner makes the next decision easier and leaves behind a process we can reuse.

One city or many

Take one Toronto mandate, a single transaction, or help build a standard that can follow the 65-city rollout.

One discipline or a coordinated team

Specialists are welcome. So are firms that can coordinate several related disciplines without blurring responsibility. Strong capital and sponsor relationships are a plus.

Paid work begins only when approved

A conversation, proposal or site submission does not authorize fees. Scope and authority must be clear before work starts.

ORDER OF EXECUTION

Control assets first. Commit capital second. Produce and sell third.

65-CITY ARCHITECTURE

Toronto proves a lane. The next city is underwritten again.

The 65-city idea survives from the earlier Capital page, but it is an operating architecture — not automatic cross-collateralization and not a promise that every city carries identical economics. Each city must earn its own property, lender, sponsor, venue, travel and operating approvals.
